svg.title: The saved Furini2016 cutting pattern in five steps
svg.desc: An original teaching comparison and a reconstruction of the archived 400-piece witness. Thirty-nine vertical cuts make forty strips; nine horizontal cuts per strip make ten pieces each. The pattern uses 399 physical cuts and 41 exact midpoint cuts, fills all 1600 area, and earns 1600 profit.
svg.text: Reconstruction of the actual saved witness
First, what makes a cut guillotine?
A full cut crosses the current rectangle.
The pinwheel has no full first boundary.
Teaching examples only, not saved decisions.
One original panel. No cuts yet.
The square has 1,600 units of area.
The cut crosses the full current panel.
Keep a 1 × 40 strip and a 39 × 40 remainder.
Repeat on the remainder for 39 cuts.
Each strip needs nine horizontal cuts.
The final 1 × 8 splits into two 1 × 4 pieces.
Final remainder shown at 5×, with true proportions.
5. The complete grid reaches the area bound
All item profits equal area, so 1,600 is the bound.
Cut order reconstructed from aggregate saved counts.
